PatientName.description: Patient first and last name, usually at the top of the page or in a demographics block. May be labeled Patient, Patient Name, Member, or appear as Last, First. On an insurance card this is the member name.

PatientDOB.description: Patient date of birth. Labeled DOB, D.O.B., Date of Birth, or Birth Date. Typically MM/DD/YYYY. Do not confuse with the date the form was written, the date of service, or a coverage effective date.

PatientGender.description: Patient gender or sex as recorded. Usually a checkbox pair labeled M/F or Male/Female, or a Sex field in a demographics header. Return Unknown if no box is marked or the marking is ambiguous.

PatientAddress.description: Patient mailing or shipping address. Often spans two lines; the second line may hold an apartment, suite, or unit number.

PatientPhone.description: Patient telephone number. Labeled Phone, Home Phone, Mobile, Cell, or Contact Number. Capture digits as printed, including area code.

PayerName.description: Insurance company, health plan, or pharmacy benefit manager name that issued or administers this document. Usually in the letterhead or the card face — for example Aetna, UnitedHealthcare, Blue Cross Blue Shield of Texas, Express Scripts, CVS Caremark, OptumRx.

MemberID.description: Insurance member or subscriber identifier. Labeled Member ID, Member #, Subscriber ID, Policy ID, Identification Number, or ID. Copy the alphanumerics exactly as printed, including any leading letters.

GroupNumber.description: Employer or plan group number. Labeled Group, Group #, Group Number, or Grp. Distinct from the member ID and from RxGroup.

RxBIN.description: Pharmacy benefit BIN, the six-digit bank identification number that routes a pharmacy claim. Labeled RxBIN, BIN, or Rx BIN. Six digits.

RxPCN.description: Pharmacy benefit processor control number. Labeled RxPCN, PCN, or Rx PCN. Alphanumeric. Frequently absent even when RxBIN is present — return null rather than reusing the BIN.

RxGroup.description: Pharmacy benefit group identifier. Labeled RxGRP, RxGroup, or Rx Group. Distinct from the medical GroupNumber, though the two sometimes match.

ProviderName.description: Prescribing or treating provider name, sometimes with a credential such as MD, DO, NP, or PA. Labeled Provider, Prescriber, Physician, Ordering Provider, or Doctor. Not the practice or facility name.

ProviderNPI.description: Prescribing provider National Provider Identifier. Always exactly 10 digits. Labeled NPI, NPI #, Provider NPI, or NPI Number. If more than one NPI appears, take the one belonging to the prescribing or ordering provider, not the facility, group or dispensing pharmacy.

ProviderDEA.description: Prescriber DEA registration number, printed near the signature line on prescriptions and enrolment forms. Two letters followed by seven digits, for example BJ1234563. Labeled DEA, DEA #, or DEA Number.

ProviderAddress.description: Provider or practice address, usually in the letterhead or prescriber block. Distinct from the patient address and from the ship-to address.

ProviderPhone.description: Provider office telephone number, from the letterhead or prescriber block. Not the fax number, and not a payer or pharmacy help-desk number.

ProviderFax.description: Fax number for the provider office, as printed. Labeled Fax, Fax #, or Fax Number. On payer correspondence this is the fax the response is to be returned to; take the provider-side number when both appear.

PrimaryDiagnosisCode.description: Primary diagnosis code, normally ICD-10-CM — a letter, two digits, then an optional dot and up to four more characters, for example M05.79 or L40.50. Labeled ICD-10, ICD, Diagnosis Code, or Dx. Where several are listed take the one marked primary, or the first if none is marked.

PrimaryDiagnosisDescription.description: Text description of the primary diagnosis as printed next to or in place of the code, for example "Rheumatoid arthritis with rheumatoid factor of multiple sites" or "Plaque psoriasis". Do not expand a code you were not given a description for.

DrugName.description: Drug or therapy name as written, brand or generic, including any strength printed alongside it — for example "Humira (adalimumab) 40 mg/0.8 mL" or "Stelara 90 mg". Copy what is on the page; reference-data resolution happens downstream.

DrugStrength.description: Strength with units as printed, for example 40 mg/0.8 mL, 90 mg/mL, or 300 mg. May be a checkbox selection rather than free text. Return null when only a drug name appears.

Signature.description: Whether a handwritten or electronic provider signature mark appears in the signature area. Detect the presence of a mark; do not transcribe a name. A printed name on the signature line with no mark over it is Absent. Text such as "Electronically signed by" is Present.

ReferralDate.description: Date the referral was completed or submitted. Labeled Date, Referral Date, or Date Submitted, usually beside the prescriber signature. Not a fax transmission timestamp printed in the page banner.

ReferralSource.description: Who sent this referral, from a "Referral Source" or "Referred By" field or from the letterhead of the sending organisation. Not documented when nothing on the page identifies the sender.

PatientEmail.description: Patient email address, where the form collects one. Copy exactly, including the domain.

PreferredLanguage.description: Patient's preferred spoken or written language, from a Preferred Language field or an interpreter-needed checkbox group.

SecondaryPayerName.description: Name of a secondary or supplemental plan, where the insurance section collects one. Null when only one plan is listed.

PatientAllergies.description: Known drug allergies as written, verbatim. NKDA and "No known drug allergies" are real values, not absences — record them as printed. Null only when the field itself is blank.

PatientWeight.description: Patient weight with units as recorded, for example 168 lb or 76.2 kg. Collected because many specialty drugs are weight-banded.

DrugDirections.description: Dosing directions or SIG, verbatim and in full. May describe loading, induction and maintenance dosing in one block. Capture the whole text rather than summarising — it is mapped to a structured SIG code downstream and the mapping needs the original wording.

Quantity.description: Quantity to dispense, with units if printed — for example 2 syringes, 4 pens, or 30 tablets.

Refills.description: Number of refills authorised, as printed. May be a numeral, a word, PRN, or NR. Null if the field is blank.

DaysSupply.description: Days supply for one fill, as printed. Labeled Days Supply or DS.

RequestedStartDate.description: Date therapy is requested to begin, or the requested delivery date. Labeled Start Date, Requested Start, or Needed By.

ShipToLocation.description: Where the medication is to be shipped, from the shipping or delivery section's checkbox group. Not documented if no box is marked.

PriorAuthorizationRequired.description: Whether a prior-authorization-required box on the form is marked, or the form states that a PA has already been initiated. Read the checkbox; do not reason about whether the drug would need one.

PatientConsentSignature.description: Whether a patient or authorised-representative signature mark appears in the consent, HIPAA authorisation or assignment-of-benefits block. Distinct from the prescriber Signature field. Detect a mark, do not transcribe a name.

InsuranceCardAttached.description: Whether the packet indicates insurance card copies are attached — either a ticked "cards attached" box or a reproduced card image on the page. No when the box is present and unticked.

DateWritten.description: Date the prescriber wrote or signed the prescription. Labeled Date, Date Written, or Date Signed. Not the patient date of birth and not the fax transmission date.

DoseForm.description: Dose form of the product ordered, from an explicit dose-form field, a checkbox group, or the form named in the drug line itself. Not documented if the order does not say.

RouteOfAdministration.description: Route the drug is to be given by, from an explicit route field or stated plainly in the directions — "inject subcutaneously" is Subcutaneous. Do not infer the route from the drug's identity.

DrugDirections.description: Dosing directions or SIG, verbatim and in full, including any loading or titration schedule. Capture the whole block rather than summarising it.

DaysSupply.description: Days supply for one fill, as printed. Labeled Days Supply or DS.

DispenseAsWritten.description: Which substitution instruction the prescriber selected. SupervisingPhysicianNPI.description: Supervising or collaborating physician NPI, printed when a nurse practitioner or physician assistant is the prescriber. Exactly 10 digits and distinct from ProviderNPI. Null when only one NPI appears.

PrescriptionOrigin.description: How the order was produced, judged from the page itself: an e-prescribing footer or "Electronically signed by" means electronic; handwritten field entries mean handwritten; a filled typed form means typed or printed. Not determinable when the scan is too poor to tell.

SubscriberName.description: Name of the policy subscriber where the card names one separately from the member. Null when only one name is printed.

PlanType.description: Plan type as printed on the card. Read the plan or product label, and any Medicare or Medicaid branding. Not documented when the card gives no indication.

PayerID.description: Electronic payer identifier for medical claims, printed on the back of many cards. Labeled Payer ID, Payor ID, or EDI Payer ID. Distinct from RxBIN, which routes pharmacy claims.

EffectiveDate.description: Date coverage takes effect, where the card prints one. Labeled Effective Date or Coverage Effective.

CopayInformation.description: The copay grid as printed, verbatim, including the labels — for example "PCP $25 / Specialist $50 / ER $250 / Rx Tier 1 $10". Capture the whole block on one line rather than picking one figure.

MemberServicesPhone.description: Member or customer services telephone number, usually on the reverse. Not the pharmacy help desk number.

PharmacyHelpDeskPhone.description: Pharmacy or provider help desk telephone number, printed beside the Rx routing numbers on the reverse. Null when only one number appears and it is labeled for members.

CardSide.description: Which faces of the card this scan reproduces. Front and back when two card rectangles appear on the page. Judge from the layout, not from which fields you managed to read.

NoteType.description: What kind of encounter this note documents, from its title or header block. Not documented when the note is untitled.

FacilityName.description: Practice, clinic or health system the note was written at, usually in the header or the EHR footer. Not the provider's personal name.

ChiefComplaint.description: The chief complaint or reason for visit, verbatim from that labeled line. Do not substitute the diagnosis.

PatientWeight.description: Patient weight with units from the vitals block, for example 168 lb or 76.2 kg.

PatientHeight.description: Patient height as recorded, for example 5 ft 9 in or 175 cm.

SecondaryDiagnoses.description: Every diagnosis listed in the note other than the primary one, from the assessment, problem list or diagnosis block. Empty array when the note lists only one.

Allergies.description: Allergies as recorded, verbatim. NKDA and "No known drug allergies" are real values — record them as printed rather than as null.

CurrentMedications.description: The current medication list as printed, one entry per line of the list, each with its strength and directions if given. Medication lists routinely straddle page breaks, so read the whole document before deciding the list has ended.

PriorTherapies.description: Therapies the patient has ALREADY tried for the condition under treatment, and what happened. This is the single most important field on this document — step-therapy criteria are decided on it. Gather from wherever the note records it: a past-medications section, the HPI narrative, or the assessment. Include only drugs described as previously tried, stopped, failed or not tolerated — not the current medication list. Empty array when the note records no prior therapy.

StepTherapyDocumented.description: Whether this note documents a trial of, and failure or intolerance to, at least one prior therapy for the condition being treated. Yes requires both the trial and its unsatisfactory outcome to be stated. A note listing prior drugs with no outcome is Not documented.

RelevantLabValues.description: Laboratory values quoted anywhere in this note — in the objective section, an embedded results table, or the narrative. Take only values actually printed in the document. Empty array when the note quotes none.

TBScreeningResult.description: Result of tuberculosis screening, which payers require before most biologics start. Infer from a QuantiFERON-TB Gold or T-SPOT result, a PPD or tuberculin skin test reading, or a chest X-ray finding, read together with the assessment. Not documented when the note is silent — that absence is itself the finding, so do not guess.

TreatmentPlan.description: The plan for this patient going forward, summarised from the plan or assessment-and-plan section — what is being started, changed, continued or ordered. Two or three sentences. Base it only on what the note states.

PerformingLabCLIA.description: CLIA certificate number of the performing laboratory, printed in the header or footer. Ten characters, typically two digits then the letter D then seven digits. Labeled CLIA or CLIA #.

LabDirector.description: Laboratory director or pathologist named on the report, usually in the footer with a credential.

AccessionNumber.description: Laboratory accession, requisition or specimen number identifying this report. Labeled Accession, Accession #, Requisition, or Specimen ID.

SpecimenType.description: Specimen material tested, from a Specimen or Source field. Not documented when the report does not say.

SpecimenCollectedDate.description: Date the specimen was collected or drawn. Labeled Collected, Collection Date, or Drawn. Not the received date and not the report date — payers date step-therapy evidence from this one.

SpecimenReceivedDate.description: Date the laboratory received the specimen. Labeled Received.

ReportDate.description: Date the report was issued or resulted. Labeled Reported, Report Date, or Final Report Date.

ReportStatus.description: Status the report declares for itself, usually printed beside the title or on each result. A corrected or preliminary report is not acceptable evidence for some payers, so read the label rather than assuming Final.

Results.description: Every row of the results table, in the order printed. One entry per analyte. Read the whole table including any rows continuing onto a second page.

AbnormalResultsPresent.description: Whether any row on the report carries an abnormal flag. Read the flag column; do not compare values against ranges yourself. Not determinable when the report prints no flag column at all.

CriticalResultsPresent.description: Whether any row is marked critical, panic, or alert, or the report records a critical-value callback. Distinct from merely abnormal.

PrimaryDiagnosisCode.description: Primary diagnosis code, normally ICD-10-CM — a letter, two digits, then an optional dot and up to four more characters, for example M05.79 or L40.50. Labeled ICD-10, ICD, Diagnosis Code, or Dx. Where several are listed take the one marked primary, or the first if none is marked.

AppealDeadlineDate.description: The calendar date by which an appeal must be filed, where the document prints one. Copy the printed date. If the document only states a window such as "within 60 days of this notice" and prints no date, this is null — do not calculate it.

LetterDate.description: Date printed on the letter itself, in the dateline. Appeal windows are usually counted from this date.

DeterminationDate.description: Date the decision was made, where the letter states one separately from the letter date. Labeled Determination Date, Decision Date, or Date of Determination. Null when only one date appears.

ReviewType.description: What kind of review produced this decision, as the letter describes it. Appeal decision when the letter is deciding an appeal of an earlier denial rather than an initial request.

ApprovalEffectiveDate.description: First date the authorization is valid. Labeled Effective Date, Valid From, or Start Date. Null on a denial.

ApprovalExpiryDate.description: Last date the authorization is valid. Labeled Valid Through, Expiry Date, End Date, or Approved Through. Null on a denial.

ApprovedQuantity.description: Quantity, units, visits or doses authorised, as printed — for example "2 syringes per 28 days". Copy the whole phrase including any period it is expressed over. Null on a denial.

ApprovedDaysSupply.description: Days supply authorised per fill, where the letter states one.

DenialReasonCode.description: The reason code the payer prints beside its denial. May be a claim adjustment reason code such as CO-50, CO-197 or PR-1, or a plan-specific code such as PA-014. Copy it exactly as printed, including any prefix and hyphen. Null when the letter gives a reason in words with no code.

enum: Prescriber or pharmacy out of network
DenialReasonCategory.description: The payer's stated grounds, mapped to the closest category. Read the rationale paragraph, not the code. Not applicable when the outcome is an approval. Use Other when the letter states a reason that fits none of these, rather than forcing the nearest one.

DenialReasonNarrative.description: Why the request was refused, summarised from the rationale section in two or three sentences. Preserve what the payer actually said — which criterion was unmet, which document was missing, which alternative had not been tried — rather than paraphrasing into a generic reason. This text is read by staff and by patients asking why they were denied, so accuracy matters more than brevity. Null on an approval.

CriteriaNotMet.description: The specific coverage criteria the letter says were not satisfied, one entry each, as the letter words them. Denial letters commonly list these as bullets under the rationale. Empty array on an approval or when the letter gives no itemised criteria.

SuggestedAlternatives.description: Formulary or preferred alternatives the letter suggests instead of the requested drug, from a "covered alternatives" or "preferred agents" section. Empty array when the letter suggests none.

MedicalPolicyReference.description: The coverage policy, criteria document or guideline the decision cites, as identified — for example "Pharmacy Policy PH-0142" or a named clinical policy bulletin. Null when the letter cites none.

AppealWindowDays.description: The number of days allowed to file an appeal, as printed — for example 60 or 180. Read the number the letter states; do not derive it from AppealDeadlineDate, and do not supply a typical value.

AppealLevel.description: The next appeal step this letter offers. Where several are described, take the first one available to the requester.

AppealRightsSummary.description: How to appeal, summarised from the appeal-rights section — who may file, by when, where to send it, and what to include. Two or three sentences. Null when the letter describes no appeal rights, which is itself notable on a denial.

AppealSubmissionFax.description: Fax number appeals are to be sent to, from the appeal-rights section. Distinct from the provider fax in the letterhead.

AppealSubmissionPhone.description: Telephone number given for appeals or for questions about the decision.

PeerToPeerOffered.description: Whether the letter offers a peer-to-peer or physician-to-physician discussion with the plan's reviewer, and usually a number or window to arrange it. Not documented when the letter does not mention one.

ExternalReviewRightsStated.description: Whether the letter describes the right to an external or independent review after internal appeals are exhausted, typically naming an independent review organisation or a state insurance department.

ReviewerName.description: Name and credential of the clinical reviewer or medical director who signed the determination, where the letter names one.

PatientName.description: Patient first and last name, usually at the top of the page or in a demographics block. May be labeled Patient, Patient Name, Member, or appear as Last, First. On an insurance card this is the member name.

PatientDOB.description: Patient date of birth. Labeled DOB, D.O.B., Date of Birth, or Birth Date. Typically MM/DD/YYYY. Do not confuse with the date the form was written, the date of service, or a coverage effective date.

MemberID.description: Insurance member or subscriber identifier. Labeled Member ID, Member #, Subscriber ID, Policy ID, Identification Number, or ID. Copy the alphanumerics exactly as printed, including any leading letters.

PayerName.description: Insurance company, health plan, or pharmacy benefit manager name that issued or administers this document. Usually in the letterhead or the card face — for example Aetna, UnitedHealthcare, Blue Cross Blue Shield of Texas, Express Scripts, CVS Caremark, OptumRx.

CaseNumber.description: Payer case, reference or tracking number for this request. Labeled Case #, Reference #, Ref #, Request ID, or Determination ID. This identifies the REQUEST; AuthorizationNumber identifies a granted authorization.

AuthorizationNumber.description: Authorization or certification number granted by the payer. Labeled Auth #, Authorization Number, Certification Number, or PA Number. Return null when nothing was authorized, even if a case number is present.

PAOutcome.description: The determination this document communicates. Read the decision sentence or the status field in the body, never the letterhead or the subject line. Partially approved covers an approval granted at a reduced quantity, duration or strength. Pending covers a request still in review or held for more information.

ProviderName.description: Prescribing or treating provider name, sometimes with a credential such as MD, DO, NP, or PA. Labeled Provider, Prescriber, Physician, Ordering Provider, or Doctor. Not the practice or facility name.

ProviderNPI.description: Prescribing provider National Provider Identifier. Always exactly 10 digits. Labeled NPI, NPI #, Provider NPI, or NPI Number. If more than one NPI appears, take the one belonging to the prescribing or ordering provider, not the facility, group or dispensing pharmacy.

ProviderFax.description: Fax number for the provider office, as printed. Labeled Fax, Fax #, or Fax Number. On payer correspondence this is the fax the response is to be returned to; take the provider-side number when both appear.

DrugName.description: Drug or therapy name as written, brand or generic, including any strength printed alongside it — for example "Humira (adalimumab) 40 mg/0.8 mL" or "Stelara 90 mg". Copy what is on the page; reference-data resolution happens downstream.

ResponseDate.description: Date the payer issued this response, from the form's date field. Not the fax transmission timestamp in the page banner.

RequestReceivedDate.description: Date the payer records having received the original request. Labeled Received, Date Received, or Request Date.

FormOrPortalName.description: Title of the response form or the portal it was printed from, as it appears at the top of the page — for example "Prior Authorization Determination Notice" or "CoverMyMeds Request Summary".

ApprovedThroughDate.description: Last date of the authorised period, where the response grants one. Null unless the outcome is an approval.

ApprovedQuantity.description: Quantity or days supply authorised, as printed, including the period it applies over.

PendingReason.description: Why the request is not yet decided. Not applicable when the response reports a final outcome. Not documented when it reports pending without saying why.

InformationRequested.description: Exactly what the payer is asking for before it will decide — chart notes for a date range, a specific lab result, a step-therapy attestation, a corrected NDC. One entry per item, worded as the form words it. This list is what a follow-up to the prescriber's office is built from, so keep each item specific enough to act on and do not merge two requests into one entry. Empty array when nothing further is requested.

ResponseDueDate.description: Date by which the requested information must be returned before the request is closed or denied. Labeled Response Due, Reply By, or Information Due.

DenialReasonCode.description: Reason code printed beside a denied outcome, exactly as it appears. Null when the outcome is not a denial or no code is given.

ContinuationOfTherapy.description: Whether this authorises continuation of therapy the patient is already receiving rather than a new start. Infer from renewal, reauthorization, or continued-use language on the form.

ReviewerName.description: Name of the reviewer, nurse or coordinator who completed the response, with any credential printed beside it.

CallbackPhone.description: Telephone number the form gives for questions about this response.

ReturnFaxNumber.description: Fax number the completed sheet or the requested information is to be returned to, usually beside a "fax this back to" instruction.

PatientName.description: Patient first and last name, usually at the top of the page or in a demographics block. May be labeled Patient, Patient Name, Member, or appear as Last, First. On an insurance card this is the member name.

PatientDOB.description: Patient date of birth. Labeled DOB, D.O.B., Date of Birth, or Birth Date. Typically MM/DD/YYYY. Do not confuse with the date the form was written, the date of service, or a coverage effective date.

MemberID.description: Insurance member or subscriber identifier. Labeled Member ID, Member #, Subscriber ID, Policy ID, Identification Number, or ID. Copy the alphanumerics exactly as printed, including any leading letters.

GroupNumber.description: Employer or plan group number. Labeled Group, Group #, Group Number, or Grp. Distinct from the member ID and from RxGroup.

PayerName.description: Insurance company, health plan, or pharmacy benefit manager name that issued or administers this document. Usually in the letterhead or the card face — for example Aetna, UnitedHealthcare, Blue Cross Blue Shield of Texas, Express Scripts, CVS Caremark, OptumRx.

ProviderName.description: Prescribing or treating provider name, sometimes with a credential such as MD, DO, NP, or PA. Labeled Provider, Prescriber, Physician, Ordering Provider, or Doctor. Not the practice or facility name.

ProviderNPI.description: Prescribing provider National Provider Identifier. Always exactly 10 digits. Labeled NPI, NPI #, Provider NPI, or NPI Number. If more than one NPI appears, take the one belonging to the prescribing or ordering provider, not the facility, group or dispensing pharmacy.

DrugName.description: Drug or therapy name as written, brand or generic, including any strength printed alongside it — for example "Humira (adalimumab) 40 mg/0.8 mL" or "Stelara 90 mg". Copy what is on the page; reference-data resolution happens downstream.

DrugNDC.description: National Drug Code for the product, 10 or 11 digits usually printed with hyphens as 5-4-2 or 5-3-2, for example 00074-3799-02. Labeled NDC or NDC #. Copy the hyphenation exactly as printed.

DateOfService.description: Date the care described in this document was delivered. Labeled Date of Service, DOS, Visit Date, Service Date, or Encounter Date. Not the date the document was printed, signed or mailed.

AppealDeadlineDate.description: The calendar date by which an appeal must be filed, where the document prints one. Copy the printed date. If the document only states a window such as "within 60 days of this notice" and prints no date, this is null — do not calculate it.

ClaimNumber.description: Claim identifier assigned by the payer. Labeled Claim #, Claim Number, ICN, or Document Control Number.

StatementDate.description: Date the statement was issued, from the header. Not the date of service.

ClaimStatus.description: How the claim was adjudicated, from the status column or the summary line. Read the status the statement prints rather than inferring it from the amounts.

PharmacyName.description: Dispensing pharmacy or servicing provider named on the claim line. Distinct from the prescriber.

PharmacyNPI.description: NPI of the dispensing pharmacy, ten digits. Distinct from ProviderNPI, which is the prescriber's.

QuantityDispensed.description: Quantity dispensed on this claim line, as printed.

DaysSupply.description: Days supply billed on this claim line, as printed.

BilledAmount.description: Amount billed or submitted, copied exactly as printed including the currency symbol and any thousands separator — for example $12,480.00. Do not reformat it into a bare number.

AllowedAmount.description: Plan-allowed or contracted amount, as printed. Labeled Allowed, Eligible, or Plan Allowance.

PlanPaidAmount.description: Amount the plan paid, as printed. Labeled Plan Paid, Payment, or Amount Paid.

PatientResponsibility.description: Total the patient owes for this claim, as printed. Labeled Patient Responsibility, You May Owe, or Member Liability. Read the printed total — never add the copay, coinsurance and deductible figures together yourself.

CopayAmount.description: Copay applied, as printed. Null when no copay line appears.

DeductibleApplied.description: Amount applied to the deductible on this claim, as printed. Not the year-to-date deductible accumulator.

AdjustmentReasonCodes.description: Claim adjustment reason codes explaining any difference between billed and paid — CARC codes such as CO-50, CO-197, PR-1 or PR-3, usually printed in a code column or a legend at the foot of the page. Copy each code exactly, with its group prefix if one is printed. Empty array when the statement shows none.

RemarkCodes.description: Remittance advice remark codes, typically N-prefixed such as N130 or N362, giving supplementary explanation. Empty array when none appear.

ClaimDenialReason.description: Why this claim was refused or reduced, summarised in one or two sentences from the codes, the legend and any narrative on the statement. Null when the claim was paid in full. Say what the statement says — do not diagnose the cause yourself.

PriorAuthorizationOnFile.description: Whether the statement indicates an authorization was on file for this claim — an authorization number printed on the line, or a code stating precertification was absent, which is No. Not documented when the statement is silent on authorization.

YearToDateDeductible.description: Year-to-date deductible accumulator, as printed in the summary or accumulator block. Null when the statement shows no accumulator.

YearToDateOutOfPocket.description: Year-to-date out-of-pocket accumulator, as printed. Null when absent.
